So before I get booed and hissed off stage, hear me out fellow watchers. Season 1 (streaming on Netflix) is, frankly, a total mess. Over written dramatics surrounding underwritten and at times pretentious and on the nose writing rules the day.

Think of it as fan fiction of someone to write a new "Don Draper" like character centered show involving 1980s computers.

The main character, played by Lee Pace, is a Gordon Gekko/Don Draper hybrid with nonsensical motivations. Not a great sales pitch am I right?

Somehow though, season 1 manages to show flashes of brilliance partly through the sheer force of Lee Pace's intensity. Despite being given poor writing to work with, he pulls it off.

Here's where things get interesting though: season 2 is a hidden gem. The show goes under a re-tool of sorts and fixes all the mistakes made the first go round. Unfortunately, season 2 is only for pay on Amazon Prime but it's really worth it. Amazingly it manages to close and continue threads from the very shaky season 1.

Also of note: it has a killer introduction scene.

I gotta say I recommend both seasons despite all the initial problems. Actually the pilot episode is pretty great but don't expect it to be that good again until season 2.
